nodes.summary: After inserting a list, bit `i` is set iff it was set before or some hash function sends some inserted element to `i`.
nodes.title: Bits set after inserting a list into a Bloom filter

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a Bloom filter over $\alpha$ with $m$ bits, let $x \in \alpha$ and let $i \in \{0, \dots, m - 1\}$. Bit $i$ of the filter obtained by inserting $x$ into $F$ is set if and only if bit $i$ of $F$ is set or some hash function $h$ of $F$ satisfies $h(x) = i$.
nodes.title: Bits set by an insertion

nodes.summary: A Bloom filter over a type $\alpha$ with $m$ bits consists of a finite list of hash functions $\alpha \to \{0, \dots, m - 1\}$ and a bit vector of length $m$.
nodes.title: Bloom filter

nodes.summary: Exactly `(m - 1) ^ (n * k)` outcomes of the stored hash values leave bit `i` unset.
nodes.title: Number of hash outcomes leaving a given bit unset

nodes.summary: Bloom's formula is a lower bound on the exact false-positive rate (Jensen's inequality for `t ↦ t ^ k`).
nodes.title: Bloom's formula is a lower bound

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type and $m$ a natural number. Given a list of hash functions $\alpha \to \{0, \dots, m - 1\}$, the empty Bloom filter with these hash functions has all of its $m$ bits unset.
nodes.title: Empty Bloom filter

nodes.summary: At `κ = (m / n) log 2` half of the bits are expected to be set and the approximation is `(1 / 2) ^ κ`.
nodes.title: Exponential approximation at the optimal number of hash functions

nodes.summary: The exponential approximation `(1 - exp (-(k n) / m)) ^ k` is also a lower bound.
nodes.title: Exponential approximation is a lower bound on the false-positive rate

nodes.summary: The optimal number of hash functions for the exponential approximation: on real `κ > 0`, `(1 - exp (-κ n / m)) ^ κ` is minimal at `κ = (m / n) log 2`.
nodes.title: The optimal number of hash functions

nodes.summary: The exponential approximation `(1 - exp (-κ n / m)) ^ κ` of the false-positive rate, as a function of a real number `κ` of hash functions.
nodes.title: Exponential approximation of the Bloom filter false-positive rate

nodes.summary: The expected fraction of set bits is `1 - (1 - 1/m) ^ (n * k)`.
nodes.title: Expected fraction of set bits in a Bloom filter

nodes.summary: The exact false-positive rate is the expectation of `(fraction of set bits) ^ k`.
nodes.title: False-positive rate as the expected k-th power of the set fraction

nodes.summary: The exact false-positive rate under uniform hashing: the fraction of outcomes (stored hash values `H`, query hash values `q`) in which every query bit is set.
nodes.title: Exact Bloom filter false-positive rate under uniform hashing

nodes.summary: Insertion keeps the hash functions.
nodes.title: Bloom filter insertion keeps the hash functions

nodes.summary: Insert every element of a list, left to right.
nodes.title: Inserting a list of elements into a Bloom filter

nodes.summary: Inserting an element $x$ into a Bloom filter keeps its hash functions and sets bit $h(x)$ for every hash function $h$ of the filter, leaving all other bits unchanged.
nodes.title: Bloom filter insertion

nodes.summary: Equality holds only at `t = 1 / 2`.
nodes.title: Equality in the log-product bound holds only at $t = 1/2$
Bound $\log t \cdot \log(1-t) \le (\log 2)^2$ on the unit interval

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type, $m$ a natural number and $H$ a nonempty list of hash functions $\alpha \to \{0, \dots, m - 1\}$. For every element $x \in \alpha$, the empty Bloom filter with hash functions $H$ reports $x$ absent.
nodes.title: The empty Bloom filter reports every element absent

nodes.summary: For a Bloom filter $F$ and an element $x$, $F$ reports that $x$ may be present if and only if bit $h(x)$ of $F$ is set for every hash function $h$ of $F$.
nodes.title: Membership query in terms of bits

nodes.summary: The false-positive event: after inserting `xs` into an empty filter, `y` is reported present iff every bit selected by `y` is selected by some stored element.
nodes.title: Characterization of the Bloom filter false-positive event

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a Bloom filter and let $x$, $y$ be elements. If $F$ reports that $x$ may be present, then so does the filter obtained by inserting $y$ into $F$.
nodes.title: Insertion preserves positive answers

nodes.summary: For every Bloom filter $F$ and element $x$, the filter obtained by inserting $x$ into $F$ reports that $x$ may be present.
nodes.title: An inserted element is reported present

nodes.summary: A Bloom filter reports that an element $x$ may be present when bit $h(x)$ is set for every hash function $h$ of the filter, and reports $x$ absent otherwise.
nodes.title: Bloom filter membership query

nodes.summary: A bit is unset iff no stored hash value selects it.
nodes.title: A Bloom filter bit is unset iff no stored hash selects it

nodes.summary: A given bit is unset with probability `(1 - 1/m) ^ (n * k)`.
nodes.title: Probability that a given Bloom filter bit is unset

nodes.summary: The bits set by the stored hash values `H a j` (element `a`, hash function `j`).
nodes.title: Bits set by the stored hash values

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
